mechanism: For fixed hold of N bars from each open, collect max upward and downward price deviations; build empirical frequency then complementary CDF P(reach ≥ level). Optimize TP as argmax(level × P(reach)); optimize SL via (max_excursion−SL)×P(not hit). Separate Buy vs Sell histograms because up/down distributions differ.
data_needed: OHLC history; hold duration N bars; per-bar max high−open and open−low (or path extrema) histograms; cumulative sums for CDF.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; N=5 bars primary example; also SL horizons 5/10/15 bars vs TP at 5.
why_new_for_mis: Turns raw path excursions into a probabilistic reachability sensor for level-touch risk—MIS can score how likely price is to travel X points within N bars, asymmetrically by side.
quote: we will obtain an estimate of the probability that the price will reach a given level

mechanism: Any trade closes at TP or SL only; P(TP)=P(reach TP)×P(not reach SL) (and symmetric for SL). Expected payoff E = TP·P(TP) − SL·P(SL). Scan (SL,TP) pairs for positive/max E, or fix one side and optimize the other. Alternate criterion: average-profit/average-loss ratio.
data_needed: Same excursion CDFs as above; candidate SL/TP grids in points.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; example optima Buy SL 622/TP 210 then EV-tuned TP 310 given SL 622.
why_new_for_mis: Joint touch-probability expected-value surface is a richer volatility/risk sensor than separate ATR stops—MIS can map which (SL,TP) regions have positive edge under empirical path law.
quote: the expected payoff equation will look like this

mechanism: Event study on final dividend announcements: split Nifty-50 names into increased/decreased/neutral vs prior dividend. AR_i,t = R_i,t − R_m,t (NSE 500 proxy). AAR_t = mean AR across group; CAAR = cumulative AAR over −15..+15 day window. Persistent non-zero AAR and trending CAAR (esp. + for increases from T−5, − for decreases through ~T+10) flags slow information incorporation.
data_needed: Daily closes of constituents + market index; dividend announcement dates and signed change class; event window ±15 trading days; t-stats on AAR.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Nifty 50 stocks (43 with 2022 final dividends: 29 up, 5 down, 9 flat); NSE 500; daily; ±15 day window.
why_new_for_mis: Corporate-action event window AAR/CAAR is an exogenous change/inefficiency sensor MIS can run around scheduled micro-shocks, not just price-technical regimes.
quote: it takes some time for the market to incorporate any new information and investors can take benefit of this information inefficiency

mechanism: Market makers normally pin tight ECN spreads; they contractually leave on holidays, abnormal activity, and news. Immediate observable: spread widens sharply. Wide spread / gaps / one-sided depth = low liquidity / MM inventory-risk regime. Simple MM EA keeps bid/ask limit ladders at Delta spacing but is illustrative only.
data_needed: Symbol spread (Ask−Bid) time series; optional depth/order-book if available; news/holiday calendar for labeled exits.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURGBP, USDJPY, EURJPY (tester Feb 2023–Feb 2024); multi-FX inputs; H1 tester context.
why_new_for_mis: Frames spread expansion explicitly as a market-maker-departure / liquidity-hole sensor rather than raw cost—actionable MIS liquidity regime flag around news and stress.
quote: We can see the market maker leaving the market immediately by the extended spread

mechanism: Build features SMA_20, RSI_20, ATR_20 on M1 closes; target = 1 if next close > close else 0. Train Quadratic Discriminant Analysis on first 4000 bars (OHLC → Target), evaluate on holdout; live loop forecasts each new bar and flips/closes when forecast opposes open side.
data_needed: MT5 symbol rates via mt5R; quantmod SMA/RSI/ATR; MASS::qda; chronological train/test split (no shuffle).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 75 Index; Boom 1000 Index mentioned; iTF=1 (M1); 5000 rows fetch, train 1:4000.
why_new_for_mis: Lightweight classical sequence classifier (QDA on OHLC±indicators) as a next-bar direction neural/statistical sensor MIS can ensemble—distinct from deep nets.
quote: If next close is greater than close our target will be one otherwise zero

mechanism: Aroon Up = 100×(n − bars_since_n_period_high)/n; Aroon Down = 100×(n − bars_since_n_period_low)/n. Oscillates 0–100. Up>Down → bullish regime; Down>Up → bearish. Regular new highs ⇒ strong uptrend; regular new lows ⇒ strong downtrend.
data_needed: High/Low series; period n (default 25); iHighest/iLowest within window.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic _Symbol; tested M15 and H1 over 2023; period 25.
why_new_for_mis: Encodes trend regime as recency-of-extrema (time fraction), not price distance—complements MA/ATR regime sensors in MIS.
quote: the strong uptrend is that we can see that it is regularly making new highs, but the strong downtrend is that it is regularly making new lows

mechanism: Change cues from Aroon Down vs fixed levels: Down crosses below 10 → buy (downtrend exhaustion); Down crosses above 50 → sell. Separate from Up/Down crossover change cue.
data_needed: Aroon Down buffer current and previous; levels 10 and 50.
why_new_for_mis: Level-cross of the down-leg of Aroon gives an asymmetric change sensor focused on downside-pressure flips.

mechanism: Middle = EMA(typical price, period); Upper = EMA + multi×ATR (or avg high−low); Lower = EMA − multi×ATR. Channel width tracks volatility. Rebound sense: close reclaim above lower / reject below upper. Breakout sense: close breaks above upper / below lower.
data_needed: iMA + iATR (or rolling H−L average); multiplier (default 2); maPeriod (article default 10).
why_new_for_mis: ATR-anchored envelope as a direct volatility-regime and break/mean-reversion boundary sensor for MIS.
quote: The Keltner Channel is that technical indicator that measures the volatility of financial assets by using the exponential moving average and the average true range

mechanism: Language tutorial covering constants (#define/const), static/dynamic/multi-dim arrays, enums, structures, typecasting, local/global/static and predefined variables (_Symbol,_Point,_Period,_Digits). No market sensing constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: n/a (EURUSD only as struct demo field)
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—pure MQL5 programming pedagogy.
quote: we will mention and dive deeper to learn more about variables and data types in MQL5

mechanism: Detect impulsive middle candle (~70% body) whose neighbors leave an unfilled wick gap: bullish FVG if low[i] > high[i+2] and gap_points > minPts; bearish if low[i+2] > high[i] and gap > minPts. Zone = rectangle between those wicks, extended FVG_Rec_Ext_Bars. Sense fill when price returns to zone (Ask < fvgLow for buy; Bid > fvgHigh for sell); truncate/expire if unfilled past extension.
data_needed: OHLC of three consecutive bars; minPts threshold (100); extension length in bars (10); object/zone store.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period on chart; strategy-tester results shown generically.
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes Smart-Money fair-value-gap as a measurable liquidity-imbalance zone sensor (size, side, fill, expiry)—not just a chart pattern label.
quote: FVGs require the appearance of a three-candle design with particular guidelines. When this occurs, the fair value gap is the area or distance between the wicks of the first and third candles

mechanism: Integer-scaled difference D ∝ N·(price − SMA)/point. Build historical histogram of D (shown non-uniform and negatively skewed on EURUSD H1, N=24). Open against extremes: D below lower 15% tail → Buy; above upper 15% → Sell; close near 45% thresholds toward median—exploiting reversion from max price–SMA dislocation rather than zero-cross.
data_needed: Price and SMA(N); point size; rolling histogram/quantiles of scaled difference; open/close percentile levels.
why_new_for_mis: Empirical distribution of price−MA residual as a dislocation sensor with percentile regimes—MIS gets non-parametric stretch/reversion state beyond z-scores.
quote: we will open positions when the difference reaches a maximum or minimum. These moments will correspond to the maximum price deviation from the SMA

mechanism: From SMA/EMA-like/SMMA-triangular/LWMA oscillators build empirical distribution functions F_i from frequencies. Combine with naive Bayes final probability from the product of per-indicator probabilities. Trade when combined P crosses thresholds; optional filter: Buy only if P rising, Sell if P falling.
data_needed: Four integer-valued oscillators + their histograms → EDFs; Bayes combiner; probability thresholds and optional ΔP filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD-style H1 examples in series of SMA strategies.
why_new_for_mis: Fuses heterogeneous MA-oscillator EDFs into one probabilistic sensing state via naive Bayes—ensemble sensing layer for MIS.
quote: the final probability is obtained from the probabilities of each indicator using the formula

mechanism: Each of N independent oscillators emits one of {open Buy, open Sell, close Buy, close Sell}. Act only if the same signal comes from more than 2/3 of sources: min_agree = floor(2N/3)+1 (for N=4 → ≥3). Avoids acting on conflicting mixed signals.
data_needed: Per-indicator signal enums from their own statistics; consensus counter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Four-indicator EA (SMA, modified EMA, SMMA-window, LWMA); EURUSD H1 context.
why_new_for_mis: Fault-tolerant multi-sensor consensus rule (Byzantine threshold) as a meta-sensing gate over disagreeing technical sensors.
quote: A signal can be considered reliable if it came from more than two-thirds of the sources

mechanism: Before entry, SpreadMonitor(intSL): if current spread > intSL × spreadfits, forbid trade. Encodes that stop distance must dominate spread or expected edge is eaten; typical spreadfits≥2.
data_needed: CSymbolInfo.Spread(); planned stop in points; user coefficient spreadfits.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY M15 fractal-break EA; 2023 full year optimization; inp_sl_in_int=2000 example.
why_new_for_mis: Liquidity quality gate as spread-to-risk ratio—MIS can block signals when transaction-cost regime is hostile relative to stop geometry.
quote: if the current spread is greater than the stop and the coefficient … prohibit trading

mechanism: On each tick after open: curr_sl_points = |SL−Open|/Point; potentialLoss = curr_sl_points × TickValueLoss × lots. If potentialLoss > riskPerDeal×slippfits AND position in loss AND SL≠0, close early—broker fill slippage inflated true risk beyond plan.
data_needed: Open price, SL, volume, TickValueLoss, profit; riskPerDeal and slippfits inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY intraday positional fractal EA; risk_per_deal=100; slippfits=2.
why_new_for_mis: Post-fill risk-inflation sensor detecting execution slippage vs intended risk—operational MIS safety/liquidity-quality feed.
quote: if the resulting stop exceeds risk per trade given the threshold value … close order

mechanism: H−L(i)=High−Low; smooth with EMA (or SMA) over smoothPeriod; CHV = 100×(EMA_HL(i) − EMA_HL(i−chvPeriod))/EMA_HL(i−chvPeriod). Rising CHV → range expanding fast; low/negative → compressed. Zero-line cross: CHV>0 buy bias / CHV<0 sell bias; optimize by requiring close vs MA direction agreement.
data_needed: High/Low; EMA/SMA of H−L; periods smoothPeriod & chvPeriod (defaults 10); optional MA of close.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; 2023-01-01..2023-12-31; CHV-only vs CHV+MA tests.
why_new_for_mis: Classic Chaikin %change-of-smoothed-range is an explicit volatility expansion/contraction oscillator MIS can use as a vol-regime sensor (gaps ignored by design).

mechanism: Train per-leg Conv1D+LSTM (120-bar close window) → ONNX models for three FX legs. Each bar infer predicted closes; form cross-rate product (e.g. pred_EURUSD×pred_USDJPY×(1/pred_EURJPY)). If product>1 and each leg’s |pred−close|/close exceeds perVar → trade “right” basket; if product<1 with mirrored varia → “left” basket. Lots scaled by predicted price ratios.
data_needed: M1 closes for three related pairs; MinMax scaling; ONNX runtimes; perVar threshold; basket P&L exit (targetProfit/maxLoss).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD–USDJPY–EURJPY and EURUSD–GBPUSD–EURGBP; M1; sample_size 200000 to 2024-03-04; test ~2024-04-03..04-21.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional FX parity residual sensed on predicted rather than spot legs—MIS multi-asset mispricing + sequence-model sensor.
quote: instead of using the actual prices we will use the predicted prices
